subcategory: medical multimodal RAG over heterogeneous report and text corpora with preference alignment
task: Medical VQA and medical report generation (radiology, ophthalmology, pathology)
problem: Medical multimodal RAG cannot retrieve effectively across heterogeneous sources: irrelevant retrieved reports hurt factuality and insufficient knowledge hurts clinical credibility.
architecture: HeteroRAG on the MedAtlas knowledge base: Modality-specific CLIPs (initialised from BiomedCLIP, trained on 1.10M radiology, 0.11M ophthalmology and 1.51M pathology image-text pairs) for report retrieval; a Multi-corpora Query Generator that writes corpus-specific queries for book, guideline, research, wiki and graph corpora; Heterogeneous Knowledge Preference Tuning aligning the Med-LVLM across modalities and sources.
retriever: ModCLIPs for image-to-report retrieval; MedCPT retriever and reranker for text corpora; one-hop graph lookup
knowledge_source: MedAtlas: multimodal report repositories plus textbook, guideline, research, Wikipedia and graph corpora
key_results: With Lingshu-7B, VQA-RAD accuracy 81.99 vs 72.79 (no retrieval) and 76.84 (MIRA); SLAKE 87.50 vs 86.06 (MMed-RAG).
Out-of-distribution OMVQA-Oph 86.00 vs 83.75 (K-LLaVA) and Quilt-VQA 72.89 vs 69.68 (FactMM-RAG).
On PathVQA, MIRA (92.10) and FactMM-RAG (91.98) remain above HeteroRAG (90.83).
Applied to LLaVA-Med-7B, OMVQA-Oph accuracy rises from 56.83 to 68.42.
strengths: Large retrieval corpora and scaled modality-specific retrievers; leakage between retrieval base and test sets removed by perceptual hashing.
Evaluated on 11 datasets in 3 modalities, including out-of-distribution sets, and transferred to three Med-LVLMs.

limitations.text: One-step retrieval only; multi-round tool use and reasoning left for future work.
Fairness, privacy and safety aspects of deployment are not studied.
Not the best on every dataset (e.g. PathVQA).

title: HeteroRAG: A Heterogeneous Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Medical Vision Language Tasks
